title: Library
lede: The project documents you gathered, in whatever format they arrived, and the wiki pages written from them. A source is kept byte for byte, and every claim on a page cites one.
emptyBody: Bring in the documents this project already has: a spec, a slide deck, a spreadsheet, a page you exported. Atlas copies them into sources/ untouched and never opens them until you ask.

sources.addTooltip: Copy documents into this folder's sources/
sources.findTooltip: Propose documents already in this folder and in the project folders you bound. Nothing is copied until you pick.

wiki.compileTooltip: Read sources and update their write-ups. Retained answers are reported for separate review and refresh.
wiki.lintTooltip: Start one agent turn that reads the wiki pages and reports disagreements, superseded claims, missing links, and names without a page. It writes nothing.
wiki.proposeTooltip: Start one agent turn that reads these pages and proposes one ontology node. The write stops at your permission card.
wiki.empty: No wiki pages yet. A page is Markdown with no kind:, in the shape wiki/_template.md holds.
wiki.offTemplateCount: {count, plural, one {# page does not fit the template} other {# pages do not fit the template}}
wiki.transfer: The coding agent sends requests directly to its provider; Atlas does not record that traffic. Valid source write-ups can be written automatically. Retained answers always need separate review.
wiki.compileFailed: Could not start the agent turn: {reason}
wiki.compileWebLimit: Writing pages needs a coding agent running on this computer, which only the app can start. Reading and editing the pages works here.
wiki.agentMissing: Connect a coding agent to check page format and compile sources into pages.
wiki.offTemplateReason: Does not fit the wiki template: {code}. Open the page to see what to change.
wiki.offTemplateAriaLabel: How this page differs from the wiki template
wiki.offTemplateBody: It is still a document and still yours to edit. Fixing what follows makes it read the same way every other page does.
wiki.originalMissing: Cites {name}, which is not in this folder.
wiki.emptyNoTemplate: No wiki pages yet, and no template in this folder. Start a wiki from Settings › Workspace: it writes wiki/_template.md, the shape every page follows.
wiki.candidatesMore: {count, plural, one {# more name} other {# more names}}
wiki.candidatesTooltip: Names the last check saw on three or more pages with no page of their own. Only what the code builds, a domain, a capability or an element, can be proposed as a node on the map; people and organisations stay names in the wiki.
wiki.fileAnswerTooltip: Write the last answer as a wiki page under wiki/answers/, with the files it cited as its sources. Judged by the same contract as every page.
wiki.fileAnswerRejected: Not filed: the answer does not fit the page contract ({code}). Ask for citations and try again.
wiki.fixTooltip: Start one agent turn that repairs this on the pages named: both values with both citations for a disagreement, the current value first for a superseded claim, links both ways for a missing link.
wiki.newPageTooltip: Start a page you write yourself: the contract's sections and created_by: human, empty until you fill it in any editor. The list updates by itself.
wiki.newPageDialogBody: Create a Markdown draft with the standard structure ready to fill in.
wiki.newPagePreviewExample: Example path until you enter a title
wiki.newPageFailed: Could not make the page. Check the folder can be written.
wiki.askNextDone: From the next page on, the card stops each write. Settings › Workspace turns it back.
wiki.undoFailed: Could not undo: the file is already gone or the folder is not writable.
wiki.linkFindingsAriaLabel: How this page connects inside the folder
wiki.linkFindingsBody: The page fits the template. What follows is about the folder: things no single page can see about itself.
wiki.fixWithAgentTooltip: Starts one agent turn that brings this page back to the template. A repaired page that fits the template is saved as it is; one that does not stops at the permission card.
wiki.fixWithAgentTooltipAsk: Starts one agent turn that brings this page back to the template. Writing stops at the permission card.
wiki.fixMyselfTooltip: Selects this page's file in Finder. Fix it in any editor and the list follows the file.
wiki.technical: Technical detail · check codes and line numbers
wiki.technicalNote: The ontology-atlas wiki-validate command and the validate_wiki tool report these same codes.

kind-present.what: This page carries the marker (kind) that puts a document on the map, and a write-up about originals does not belong on the map.
kind-present.do: Delete that line, or move the file out of the wiki folder if it really is a concept.

missing-field.what: The info block at the top of the file has no {field} line.

section-order-missing.what: The page needs all five sections and {missing} is not there.
section-order-missing.do: Add the missing section, heading alone if you like. "Nothing here" is itself something a reader learns.

section-order-sequence.what: The sections are in a different order: right now it reads {found}.

uncited-fact.what: No original backs up what is written at {where}.
uncited-fact.do: Point it at one place in one original, or move it into the Not in sources section at the end of the page if you cannot.

bad-citation.what: A citation at {where} cannot be read.
bad-citation.do: Make it name the original file and the place inside it. The exact shape is under the technical detail.

bad-truncation-record-shape.what: The line that records how far an original was read (sources_truncated) is not a list of paths.
bad-truncation-record-shape.do: Write the path of each original that was read only in part, as a list.

bad-truncation-record-path.what: {path} is recorded as read only in part, but it is not among the originals this page uses.
bad-truncation-record-path.do: Add it to the list of originals, or remove that line.

citation-target-missing-folder.what: {path} is cited but that file is not in this folder.
citation-target-missing-folder.do: A citation a reader cannot open is not a citation: put the file in this folder, or fix the citation.

citation-target-missing-sources.what: {path} is cited but it is not among the originals this page uses.
citation-target-missing-sources.do: Add it to the list of originals, or fix the citation.

describes-needs-approval.what: This page says it speaks for a concept (describes), and that is a claim about the map a person has to confirm.
describes-needs-approval.do: Read it and set the status to reviewed, or remove that line.

dangling-wikilink.what: The link at {where} points at {target}, and there is no such page in this folder.
dangling-wikilink.do: Link to a page that exists, or write that page.

orphan-page.what: No other page points at this one yet.
orphan-page.do: Link it from the page that talks about its topic and it becomes easy to find.

shared-source-unlinked.what: {other} is written from the same original ({sources}), and neither page points at the other.
shared-source-unlinked.do: Link one of them to the other.

graph.title: Graph
graph.counts: {sources, plural, one {# source} other {# sources}} · {pages, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}} · {concepts, plural, one {# concept} other {# concepts}} · {cites, number} cites · {mentions, number} mentions
graph.countsIsland: {sources, plural, one {# source} other {# sources}} · {pages, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}} · {cites, number} cites
graph.empty: Nothing to draw yet. Once Compile writes a page, this shows which source it was written from and which concepts it names.
graph.canvasAria: The library graph: raw sources, wiki pages, and the concepts those pages name.
graph.legend: Sources stand on the left, the pages written from them beside, and the concepts those pages name on the right; the lines run from a source to the page that read it. A filled circle is a page, a square a source, a ring a concept on the map. A thicker line is a citation, a dashed one a mention. Scroll to zoom, drag the background to move, press a dot for a card beside it.
graph.legendShort: A circle is a page, a square a source, a ring a concept.
graph.legendCardOpen: A filled circle is a page, a square a source, a ring a concept on the map. A thicker line is a citation, a dashed one a mention, either way. Press Escape, or the same dot again, to close the card.
graph.legendShortCardOpen: A circle is a page, a square a source, a ring a concept. Escape closes the card.
graph.legendIslands: Past a few hundred files the picture is a map of islands: each island is one concept and the pages that name it, with the files those pages were written from packed around them. Unsorted holds pages naming no concept; Unread is the band under the islands: files no page has read yet. An amber dot is a page whose files changed since it was written. Scroll to zoom in until names appear; press a dot for a card beside it.
graph.describeIsland: {name}: an island of {pages, number} pages and the {sources, number} files they read. Press it to open them as columns; zoom in for their names.
graph.announceIsland: Island {name}, {position, number} of {total, number}: {pages, number} pages and {sources, number} files. Enter opens it as columns.
graph.describeUnread: Unread: {sources, number} files no page has read yet. Press it for where to start.
graph.unreadPressed: {sources, number} files no page has read yet, so there is nothing between them to draw. Each is marked not compiled in the Sources list; Compile next, above the picture, starts on the first.
graph.keys: Arrow keys move between dots, Enter opens a card beside the one you are on, Escape closes it.
graph.fitDone: The whole picture is already framed

describe.source: {name}: an original file. A thick line leads to the page written from it; no line means nobody has written it up yet. Press for a card beside it.
describe.page: {name}: a wiki page. Thick lines lead to the originals it cites, dashed lines to concepts it names. Press for a card beside it.
describe.concept: {name}: a concept on the map. The dashed lines lead to the wiki pages it names or was drawn from. Press for a card beside it.

describeOpen.source: {name}: an original file. A thick line leads to the page written from it; no line means nobody has written it up yet. Its card is open beside it: Escape, or press again, closes it.
describeOpen.page: {name}: a wiki page. Thick lines lead to the originals it cites, dashed lines to concepts it names. Its card is open beside it: Escape, or press again, closes it.
describeOpen.concept: {name}: a concept on the map. The dashed lines lead to the wiki pages it names or was drawn from. Its card is open beside it: Escape, or press again, closes it.

answers.title: Questions you return to
answers.lede: Keep an answer, its sources and unresolved questions together. Return when the evidence changes.
answers.empty: Ask about your documents, then choose File the answer in the conversation. Your saved questions will appear here.
answers.provenance: Source observations show changes in files. They do not verify an answer or prove which bytes the agent read.

state.rewritten: A cited original changed and this answer was rewritten from that version

answers.older: This is an earlier retained answer. Return to questions to see later revisions.
answers.refreshUnavailable: Refresh needs a connected coding agent in the desktop app. You can still read the answer, sources and previous versions here.

history.unmeasured: The previous text was not recorded for comparison.
history.matches: Previous version matches the text used for this revision.
history.changed: The previous version was edited after this revision was prepared.

answers.compareHint: Check the sources, human notes and unresolved questions. Saving creates a new draft and keeps the previous page.

answers.removedLines: {count, number} earlier lines removed or reworded
answers.saved: New answer draft saved. The previous version is preserved.
answers.savedNeedsReview: Draft saved, but its comparison inputs need another check. Both versions are preserved.
answers.refreshHint: Sends a draft request to your connected coding agent and its provider. The agent keeps its existing folder permissions. Atlas files the new draft when you compare and choose Save as new draft.
answers.refreshBlockedHistory: Revision history needs review. The link to earlier versions is not valid, so a refresh cannot be asked for. Fix answer_thread in the info block at the top of the file, then reopen this answer.
answers.refreshFailed: The refresh draft could not be requested. Try again in a moment.
